name: McBRIDE, the Hon. Emma Margaret

headline.note: Official material establishes public-hospital pharmacy employment at Wyong Hospital and Central Coast Local Health District from 2006 until entry to Parliament in 2016, with overlapping specialist, chief-pharmacist and deputy-director titles. Earlier pharmacy work in Australia and England is described but employers, dates and sectors are not identified. None of the reviewed sources establishes hours, leave or substantive full-time status, so no public or private duration is inferred.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary biography identifies the BPharm and McBride's first speech says she left the Central Coast to study pharmacy. Enrolment and completion dates, load and work overlap are not published in the reviewed sources. Her public professional post confirms she was a pharmacy student undertaking a placement in 1996; this is a study milestone, not the degree start or finish.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: First-person public post identifies a placement during 1996. Host, exact dates, pay and hours unknown; the year does not imply a year-long placement.
career_spells.counting_note: Student placement excluded pending evidence of a distinct paid employment arrangement.

career_spells.role: Graduate Diploma in Public Sector Management student
career_spells.evidence_note: The qualification and institution are published, but dates, study load and overlap with pharmacy employment are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Pharmacist, including work in Australia and Oxford, England
career_spells.evidence_note: McBride's 2016 first speech says she had worked in health for 20 years and had lived and worked in Forbes, North Sydney, Newtown, Berkeley Vale, Belmont and Oxford during her twenties. Official biographies describe health-sector work in Australia and abroad. They do not identify employers, job dates, sectors, hours or leave, and the 20-year statement is not converted into a start date. First speech describes an overseas locum post in mental health. A 2023 ministerial transcript separately confirms community pharmacy experience. Neither identifies individual employers or dates; these are components of the existing early-career span, not extra additive durations. A19December2025 government interview specifically identifies NHS mental-health work. The service setting is now identified, but the employing NHS trust versus locum agency remains unknown; the aggregate early-career sector stays unknown and is not converted into a public full-time interval.
career_spells.counting_note: Unidentified employers and undated work cannot be allocated to the public or private headline.

career_spells.employer: Wyong Hospital — NSW public health service (successive area/network/district administrations)
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen and current parliamentary biographies give the 2006–2015 specialist role. Australian Government and member biographies place the work at Wyong Hospital within Central Coast Local Health District. Exact appointment and cessation dates, classification, hours, leave and overlap with later titles are unresolved. State archives distinguish Northern Sydney-Central Coast Area Health Service to January 2011, Central Coast Local Health Network January–June 2011, then Central Coast Local Health District from July 2011. The 2013 bank director profile lists both pharmacy titles contemporaneously; exact allocation of functions remains unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: The employer was NSW-government controlled, but year-only boundaries and missing full-time evidence prevent a public-sector duration.

career_spells.employer: Wyong Hospital — NSW public health service (successive area/network/district administrations)
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies record chief-pharmacist service from 2008 to 2016, overlapping the specialist mental-health pharmacist range. Exact title-change date, whether the specialist function continued concurrently, classification, hours, leave and cessation date are unresolved. State archives distinguish Northern Sydney-Central Coast Area Health Service to January 2011, Central Coast Local Health Network January–June 2011, then Central Coast Local Health District from July 2011. The 2013 bank director profile lists both pharmacy titles contemporaneously; exact allocation of functions remains unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: A senior title does not establish substantive full-time status; the overlap must not be double-counted.

career_spells.employer: NSW Health Service — Central Coast Local Health District
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies place this role in 2016 immediately before Parliament. Removed the election day as a purported exact employment endpoint: election only bounds the transition. Appointment and cessation days, hours, campaign leave and overlap with chief-pharmacist duties remain unknown. State archives describe district staff as employed through NSW Health Service.
career_spells.counting_note: Public control is clear, but the mixed-precision boundary and missing hours prevent a countable interval.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography and Central Coast Heart profile record council service from 2008 to 2012. Council minutes of 22 August 2012 state that McBride would not contest the 8 September election. Exact commencement date, allowance and workload are unresolved; the role overlapped public-hospital employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Local elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Wyong Town Financial Services Limited — Wyong Community Bank branch of Bendigo Bank
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biography labels the directorship voluntary, ending in 2013. The 2013 company annual report dates joining to August 2009 and records 12 of 12 board meetings attended. Appointment day, resignation day and workload remain unknown; attendance is not employment hours.
career_spells.counting_note: Volunteer governance is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Public election records and secondary chronology identify Labor selection on 7 August and the federal election on 7 September 2013. Campaign remuneration, hours and leave from hospital work are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies list a Central Coast Heart Netball Premier League board role in 2016. The organisation's current profile documents McBride's long netball association and patronage but does not establish board dates, remuneration or workload.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit sporting governance is excluded from the narrow employment headline.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official records establish election on 2 July 2016 after renewed Labor candidacy. Preselection date, campaign remuneration, hours and arrangement with Central Coast Local Health District are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official records establish House service from 2 July 2016. Shadow and assistant-ministerial responsibilities are nested within elected office.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The 2013 annual-report biography records patronage distinct from the later Central Coast Heart board. Dates, pay and workload unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Community patronage/volunteering excluded from employment headline.

career_spells.employer: Toowoon Bay Surf Life Saving Club
career_spells.evidence_note: First-person conference biography describes surf lifesaving patrols. Landcare activity formerly grouped here is now separated using a publicly indexed start month. Patrol commencement, pay and hours are not inferred from the2020 bronze-medallion course.
career_spells.counting_note: Community patronage/volunteering excluded from employment headline.

career_spells.evidence_note: Professional profile lists Landcare volunteer fromSeptember2020 to present; earlier conference biography names Long Jetty. Month is self-reported, not independently confirmed. Volunteer work is excluded; no personal hours inferred.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.role: Pharmacist administering vaccinations during COVID — paid or voluntary basis unresolved
career_spells.evidence_note: In her17May2023 official press conference McBride states she gave jabs during COVID. The original transcript establishes personal clinical activity beyond a generic credential or policy appearance, but not employer, precise dates, pay, hours or regular appointment. Vaccination is recorded separately from pre-Parliament hospital roles; no continuous hospital employment, public employer or unpaid status inferred. Pandemic timing is not converted into invented2020–2022 boundaries.
career_spells.counting_note: No public/private full-time interval until employer, dates, substantive hours and paid/voluntary arrangement are supported. Any Parliament overlap remains excluded for elected service; do not double-count clinical and elected roles.

research_notes: Wyong Hospital and Central Coast Local Health District are classified as NSW public-sector employers; the three official title ranges overlap and are not added together.
McBride's first-person statement of 20 years in health is retained as context, not converted into an invented start date or full-time duration.
Earlier pharmacist employers in Australia and England remain unidentified, preventing sector allocation.
Council service, volunteer company governance, sporting governance, candidacy and federal elected office are separated from paid employment and excluded under the codebook.
No public or private full-time total is calculated because hours, leave and exact title/employment transitions remain unsupported.

2026-10-01 follow-up adds the 1996 placement milestone, overseas locum and community-pharmacy detail, August 2009 bank appointment, concurrent-title evidence and distinct community activities. Corrected unknown early employers from excluded to unknown sector and removed election day as a hospital cessation date.

State archives support successive public hospital administrations; their change dates are not new personal employment boundaries. Searched employer reports, Oxford/Forbes leads, professional profiles, full-time and campaign leave wording. LinkedIn profile returned 999 but the public placement post was accessible. APH speech direct retrieval returned 403 while indexed passages remained available; 2014 bank report URL was inaccessible. Same-name overseas researchers, lawyers and other profiles were excluded. No hours inferred from seniority, rounded experience or board attendance.

Second follow-up2October2026 identifies NHS as overseas mental-health service setting and dates the separately recorded Landcare volunteering toSeptember2020. Public professional index adds short-course leads: pharmacy business management NSW1997; mental-health first aid2018; Woolcock nicotine-addiction/smoking-cessation and PSA immunisation2019; Surf Life Saving NSW bronze medallion2020. These do not date paid practice. A designer-hosted2015 SHPA handbook reproduction identifies a3449-dollar pharmacoeconomics grant for Adelaide Health Economics semester2; attendance/completion needs original evidence. Oxford/Forbes hospital, employer, graduation and full-time queries did not resolve employers or hours.1997 in the profile belongs to a course, not a verified degree graduation. Same-name UK technician, Scottish social-care manager and overseas researchers excluded. No totals calculated.

3October2026 focused follow-up on original SHPA2015 award/course records, bank resignation and named early-pharmacy/Oxford employers found a public self-profile award entry corroborating Pharmacoeconomics Grant2015. No original SHPA grant record, funded-course attendance, leave, bank cessation day or early employer was established. Existing same-name researcher exclusions retained. This corroboration/search log is not counted as material employment enrichment; preserve original grant/course gap and avoid repeating these exhausted searches without a new lead.

Fourth follow-up4October2026 used exact Oxford/NHS, Wyong Hospital and NSW Health queries. Results repeated the already recorded NHS setting, official Wyong title ranges, first-speech rounded chronology and 2011 bank-report observations. No NHS trust/agency, early pharmacy employer, hospital personnel boundary, hours or leave emerged; a same-name UK pharmacy technician was excluded.

Follow-up2026-10-04: New targeted avenue: contemporary pharmacy/formulary and Oxfordshire mental-health references, early-career 1999/2001/2003 publications and personal full-time wording. No attributable NHS trust, locum agency or early NSW employer emerged. Full-time search hits referred to other people, job advertisements or patients; do not transfer their hours to McBride. Clinical/conference material repeats Wyong and deputy-director chronology without personnel dates/leave. No original SHPA award attendance or funded-study leave identified; previously recorded grant remains a lead. Defer generic name and Oxford searches until an original employer or personnel lead is available.

Follow-up2026-10-05: Original Department of Health17May2023 transcript records her personal COVID vaccination work, added as separately identified clinical activity with unknown employer, sector, dates, paid/voluntary basis and hours. Targeted vaccination-provider, volunteer and2013 campaign-leave searches through two engines did not resolve terms; unrelated US lawyer, UK consultant and pharmacy job adverts excluded. Pharmacy policy fee comparisons, campaign donations and grant amounts are not individual pay or work hours. Generic pandemic years not assigned as boundaries. Next useful route is a personally attributable vaccination-provider appointment or volunteer record and original hospital campaign-leave record. No headlines calculated. Recovered publishing helper state loss and parse/verification-shape errors while saving previous McBain record; remote tree hashes matched both validated local files before processing this member.

Second targeted primary pass2026-10-05: Followed specific2015 SHPA Novartis Pharmacoeconomics grant lead through original conference-handbook and Adelaide course records. No attributable original award/course-attendance or hospital study-leave record emerged; search returned2022 conferences, unrelated Doreen McBride research and general economics records. Held design-portfolio draft and indexed self-reported award remain leads, not proof of study attendance/completion or leave. New original Guild3November2021 presentation https://www.guild.org.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0024/115188/Vaccination-Rollout-3rd-November.pdf identifies McBride as special guest/pharmacist and lists institutional vaccination totals, but supplies no personal clinical provider or working arrangement. AJP10November2021 article https://ajp.com.au/news/the-time-for-cupcakes-and-applause-is-over/ exposes only policy-support introduction then registered-user wall; no inaccessible continuation adopted or bypassed. Do not turn policy fee advocacy, pharmacy-wide totals or guest credentials into personal pay or hours. Vaccination-provider and grant/leave evidence remain unresolved; future useful route is attributable original provider roster or award-completion record.
open_questions: Which employers, roles and dates correspond to the Forbes, North Sydney, Newtown, Berkeley Vale, Belmont and Oxford work, and were they public or private?
What were the exact appointments, classifications, hours, leave and title transitions at Wyong Hospital and Central Coast Local Health District from 2006 to 2016?
Did the specialist mental-health pharmacist function continue concurrently after appointment as chief pharmacist in 2008?
When did the deputy-director appointment begin and hospital employment cease relative to preselection, campaigning and the 2 July 2016 election?
What were the dates, remuneration and workload for Central Coast Heart governance, and did any other professional or nonprofit roles overlap hospital work?
What leave or work arrangements applied during the 2013 and 2016 federal campaigns?
Which organisation hosted the 1996 placement, and was it separately paid employment or a study requirement?
Which employer or agency engaged McBride for the overseas mental-health locum post and community pharmacy work?
Can hospital personnel records establish continuity, legal employer and leave across the 2011 administrative changes?
Can bank records establish the exact 2013 directorship cessation and distinguish Wyong District Netball patronage from Central Coast Heart roles?
Which NHS trust or locum agency employed McBride in the UK, with what dates and hours?
Can original SHPA2015 award and University of Adelaide records establish whether the funded Health Economics study occurred and whether it involved leave from hospital employment?
Which service provider engaged McBride to administer vaccinations during COVID, when, on what paid/voluntary basis and hours, and did it involve separate clinical employment alongside Parliament?
